summary: Riker and the new Bobs Charles and Arthur organize a rescue effort for the surviving human enclaves on Earth. Their two-week survey finds about fifteen million people scattered among almost forty marked locations. USE colony ships can carry ten thousand people in stasis, making the evacuation a fifteen-hundred-ship-or-trip problem, while HEAVEN vessels cannot land or enter an atmosphere. Scavenging autofactories are operating and a shipyard autofactory is hoped within two years; Riker shifts manufacturing toward transport, and Butterworth agrees that refugees may occupy his group's compound after its departure. Arthur begins outreach with manufactured communicators, but only about a quarter have been delivered or attempted and some groups resist contact.

updates.state: Cloud and dust obscure a heavily damaged surface; asteroid strikes and nuclear weapons have disrupted weather patterns, and dozens of impact sites are visible. A survey estimates that about fifteen million people remain, scattered among almost forty marked locations, and recovery is expected to take five to ten thousand years.

updates.description: A converted interplanetary freighter equipped as a Von Neumann probe: a small, light, resilient design built to copy itself. It carries a SURGE drive ring, fusion reactor, ramscoop, three large 3D printers, ROAMers, nanites and mining cargo carriers, but no weapons. Version-2 HEAVENs add a larger reactor and drive, better reactor shielding, a rail-gun, ship-busters, bigger replicant systems and more cargo room. Its communications report to Earth and were not built for interstellar conversation. HEAVEN vessels are not designed to land or enter an atmosphere.

A planned USE colony ship designed by refugee scientists as an off-world refuge. Its plans require a space-based construction yard and a viable destination. It can carry ten thousand people at a time in stasis pods.
